title: MR02 10-round AES-128 Sparse quadratic AES key-schedule system

target.description: Standard full10-round AES128 embedded in BES overGF(2^8), restricted to the AES conjugacy image BA. BES alone has a128-byte state, not the16-byte AES state.

setting.key_relation: One ordinary AES128 master key; embedded schedule must retain conjugacy and the actual AES key-schedule constraints.
setting.plaintext_model: AES16-byte plaintext/key and their conjugate embeddings; never arbitrary unrelated BES state/key vectors.
assumptions: No zero inversion in encryption OR key schedule, as required by Section6.1.
Source separately estimates53% encryptions and85% AES128 keys satisfy respective no-zero conditions; no independent joint probability is asserted.
AES conjugacy constraints included; encryption and schedule share1408 basic key coordinates.

The displayed53%/85% fractions agree numerically with independent-byte heuristics (255/256)^160 and (255/256)^40, but this local arithmetic does not prove independence or a joint attack success probability.

limitations: PDF pp.13–14 Section6.2 offers a speculative2^100 XSL estimate and immediately notes the independent-equation estimate appears inaccurate. It is not admitted as a feasible AES attack or attack time. No AES192/256 numeric projection.

Later primary analyses distinguish compact XSL from ePrint-XSL/BES and identify deficient independence/solvability estimates. They do not invalidate the existence of this representation or establish that every algebraic solver is ineffective.

property.statement: The source sparse AES128 key-schedule system has2560 equations overGF(2^8):960 quadratic+1600 linear,2368 terms and2048 variables=1408 basic-key+640 auxiliary variables. The1408 key variables overlap those of the encryption system, so naive addition would double-count them.
property.quantifier: Source AES128 GF(2^8) representation with conjugacy and no-zero inversions in encryption and key schedule.
property.scope: Equation/term/variable counts describe an algebraic system. No efficient solved-system algorithm or key-recovery resource bound is established.
